value.en: Yang Fei; Lu Qian; Cui Jie; Lu Shuowu; Yang Xiuzhi; Yuan Yuxiu
value.literal: Yang Fei; Lu Qian; Cui Jie; Lu Shuowu; Yang Xiuzhi; Yuan Yuxiu

value.zh: 潛從祖兄懷仁，字子友，魏司徒司馬道將之子。
value.en: Qian's second cousin Huainian, styled Ziyou, was son of Wei secretariat marshal Daojiang.
value.literal: Qian's second cousin Huainian, styled Ziyou, was son of Wei secretariat marshal Daojiang.

value.zh: 懷仁涉學有文辭，情性恬靖，常蕭然有閑放之致。
value.en: Huainian was broadly learned with literary accomplishment; his nature was calm and quiet, often bearing an air of leisurely detachment.
value.literal: Huainian was broadly learned with literary accomplishment; his nature was calm and quiet, often bearing an air of leisurely detachment.

value.zh: 歷太尉記室、弘農郡守，不之任，卜居陳留界。
value.en: He served as recorder for the grand commandant and as administrator of Hongnong but did not take up the post, choosing residence on the border of Chenliu.
value.literal: He served as recorder for the grand commandant and as administrator of Hongnong but did not take up the post, choosing residence on the border of Chenliu.

value.zh: 所著詩賦銘頌二萬餘言，又撰《中表實錄》二十卷。
value.en: His writings in poetry, fu, eulogy, and hymn exceeded twenty thousand words; he also compiled Records of Kindred Excellence in twenty scrolls.
value.literal: His writings in poetry, fu, eulogy, and hymn exceeded twenty thousand words; he also compiled Records of Kindred Excellence in twenty scrolls.

value.zh: 懷仁有行檢，善與人交，與瑯邪王衍、隴西李壽之情好相得。
value.en: Huainian had conduct and probity and was good at friendship; with Langye Wang Yan and Longxi Li Shou he was deeply close.
value.literal: Huainian had conduct and probity and was good at friendship; with Langye Wang Yan and Longxi Li Shou he was deeply close.

value.zh: 曾語衍云：「昔太丘道廣，許劭知而不顧；
value.en: He once told Yan, "In antiquity Taichiu's way was broad yet Xu Shao knew him and would not look at him;
value.literal: He once told Yan: "In antiquity Taichiu's way was broad yet Xu Shao knew him and would not look at him;

value.zh: 嵇生性惰，鐘會過而絕言。
value.en: Ji's nature was indolent yet Zhong Hui passed by and broke off speech with him.
value.literal: Ji's nature was indolent yet Zhong Hui passed by and broke off speech with him.

value.zh: 吾處季、孟之間，去其泰甚。」
value.en: I stand between Chi and Meng and have removed their excesses."
value.literal: I stand between Chi and Meng and have removed their excesses."

value.zh: 愆以為然。
value.en: Yan thought it so.
value.literal: Yan thought it so.

value.zh: 武平末卒。
value.en: He died late in Wuping.
value.literal: He died late in Wuping.

value.en: Volume 84, the fifty-fourth biography: Zhai Fangjin.
value.literal: Volume 84, Biography the Fifty-Fourth: Zhai Fangjin.

value.zh: 莽聞之，大懼，乃拜其黨親輕車將軍成武侯孫建為奮武將軍，光祿勳成都侯王邑為虎牙將軍，明義侯王駿為強弩將軍，春王城門校尉王況為震威將軍，宗伯忠孝侯劉宏為奮衝將軍，中少府建威侯王昌為中堅將軍，中郎將震羌侯竇兄為奮威將軍，凡七人，自擇除關西人為校尉軍吏，將關東甲卒，發奔命以擊義焉。
value.en: Mang was terrified. He commissioned seven kinsmen and allies: Sun Jian, Marquis of Chengwu, as Raising Martial general; Wang Yi, Marquis of Chengdu, as Tiger Fang general; Wang Jun, Marquis of Mingyi, as Strong Crossbow general; Wang Kuang, commandant of the Chunwang Gate, as Shaking Awe general; Liu Hong, Marquis of Loyal Filial Piety, as Raising Assault general; Wang Chang, Marquis of Jianwei, as Center Hard general; and Dou Xiong, Marquis Who Shakes the Qiang, as Raising Might general. Mang personally picked officers from west of the passes as colonels and staff, mobilized armored troops from the east, and called out every emergency levy to crush Yi.
value.literal: When Mang heard it, he was greatly afraid; thereupon he appointed his faction and kin—Light Chariot general Marquis of Chengwu Sun Jian as Raising Martial general, Superintendent of the Household Marquis of Chengdu Wang Yi as Tiger Fang general, Marquis of Mingyi Wang Jun as Strong Crossbow general, Spring Gate Commandant of the Gates Wang Kuang as Shaking Awe general, Minister of the Imperial Clan Marquis of Loyal Filial Piety Liu Hong as Raising Assault general, Privy Treasurer Jianwei Marquis Wang Chang as Center Hard general, Gentleman of the Palace Marquis Who Shakes the Qiang Dou Xiong as Raising Might general—in all seven men; he himself chose and appointed men from west of the passes as colonels and army clerks, led east-of-the-pass armored soldiers, and issued emergency call-ups to strike Yi.

value.zh: 復以太僕武讓為積弩將軍屯函谷關，將作大匠蒙鄉侯逯並為橫野將軍屯武關，羲和紅休侯劉歆為揚武將軍屯宛，太保後丞丞陽侯甄邯為大將軍屯霸上，常鄉侯王惲為車騎將軍屯平樂館，騎都尉王晏為建威將軍屯城北，城門校尉趙恢為城門將軍，皆勒兵自奮。
value.en: He also named Grand Coachman Wu Rang Piled Crossbow general at Hangu Pass; Court Architect Lu Bing, Marquis of Mengxiang, as Transverse Wild general at Wu Pass; Liu Xin, Hongxiu marquis and minister of the calendar, as general displaying martial prowess at Nanyang; Zhen Han, Marquis of Chengyang, as grand general at Bashang; Wang Yun, Marquis of Changxiang, as chariot-and-cavalry general at Pingle Lodge; Cavalry Commandant Wang Yan as Establishing Might general north of the walls; and Gate Commandant Zhao Hui as gate general. Each braced his command for battle.
value.literal: Again he made Grand Coachman Wu Rang Piled Crossbow general to garrison Hangu Pass, Court Architect Marquis of Mengxiang Lu Bing Transverse Wild general to garrison Wu Pass, Minister of the Calendar Hongxiu Marquis Liu Xin General Who Displays Martial Prowess to garrison Wan, Grand Guardian and Rear Chancellor Marquis of Chengyang Zhen Han grand general to garrison Bashang, Marquis of Changxiang Wang Yun chariot and cavalry general to garrison Pingle Lodge, Cavalry Commandant Wang Yan Establishing Might general to garrison north of the city, Commandant of the Gates Zhao Hui Gate general—all tightened troops and roused themselves.

value.zh: 武皇帝諱炎，字安世，文帝長子也。
value.en: The emperor honored posthumously as Wu bore the personal name Yan and the courtesy name Anshi; he was the firstborn son of Emperor Wen (Sima Zhao).
value.literal: The Martial Emperor's taboo name was Yan, his style name Anshi; he was the eldest son of Emperor Wen.

value.zh: 寬惠仁厚，沈深有度量。
value.en: Broad-minded, humane, and gentle by nature, he was grave and self-contained, with the measured bearing of a true ruler.
value.literal: He was generous, kind, and humane in his magnanimity, deep and reserved, with breadth of mind.

value.zh: 魏嘉平中，封北平亭侯，歷給事中、奉車都尉、中壘將軍，加散騎常侍，累遷中護軍、假節。
value.en: During Wei’s Jiaping years he received the Beipingting marquisate and rose through a string of palace and guard posts—gentleman in attendance, commandant of the imperial chariots, general of the central rampart, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary—until he became central protector, bearing the credential staff.
value.literal: In the Jiaping era of Wei he was enfeoffed as marquis of Beipingting, then served successively as gentleman in attendance, commandant of the imperial chariots, general of the central rampart, with additional appointment as regular palace attendant of cavalier, and was repeatedly promoted to central protector with plenary authority.

value.zh: 迎常道鄉公於東武陽，遷中撫軍，進封新昌鄉侯。
value.en: At Dongwuyang he received the duke of Changdaoxiang, was named central commander of the army, and was promoted to marquis of Xinchang.
value.literal: He welcomed the duke of Changdaoxiang at Dongwuyang, was transferred to central commander of the army, and advanced to enfeoffment as marquis of Xinchang.

value.zh: 及晉國建，立爲世子，拜撫軍大將軍，開府、副貳相國。
value.en: When the Jin state was founded, he was established as heir apparent, appointed Great General Who Pacifies the Army with an office of his own, and made second-in-command assisting the Minister of State.
value.literal: When the state of Jin was founded he was established as heir apparent, appointed great general who pacifies the army with independent command, and served as deputy to the minister of state.

value.zh: 斬吳江陵都督伍延 「伍延」，各本皆作「王延」。
value.en: For beheading Wu’s Jiangling commander Wu Yan, editions all write "Wang Yan" for "Wu Yan."
value.literal: Regarding beheading Wu’s Jiangling commander Wu Yan: editions all write Wang Yan instead of Wu Yan.

value.zh: 按：本書杜預傳、吳志孫皓傳、冊府一二一、通鑑八一皆作「伍延」，今據改。
value.en: Note: Du Yu’s biography in this book, Wu zhi, Sun Hao biography, Cefu 121, and Tongjian 81 all write "Wu Yan"; it is now corrected accordingly.
value.literal: Comment: Du Yu’s biography, Wu zhi, Cefu yuangui 121, and Zizhi tongjian 81 all have Wu Yan; emend accordingly.

value.zh: 參周校及洪頤烜諸史考異。
value.en: See Zhou and Hong for discussion.
value.literal: See Zhou’s collation and Hong Yixuan’s Zhu shi kaoyi.

value.zh: 孝惠皇帝諱衷，字正度，武帝第二子也。
value.en: Emperor Hui, whose personal name was Sima Zhong and courtesy name Zhengdu, was Emperor Wu’s second son.
value.literal: The Filial and Kind Emperor, taboo name Zhong, courtesy name Zhengdu, was the second son of Emperor Wu.

value.zh: 泰始三年，立爲皇太子，時年九歲。
value.en: In 267, when he was nine years old, he was named heir apparent.
value.literal: In the third year of Taishi, he was established as crown prince; at the time he was nine sui.

value.zh: 太熙元年四月己酉，武帝崩。
value.en: In the fourth month of the first year of Taixi, on the day jiyou, Emperor Wu died.
value.literal: In the first year of Taixi, on the jiyou day of the fourth month, Emperor Wu died.

value.zh: 是日，皇太子即皇帝位，大赦，改元爲永熙。
value.en: That same day the heir apparent ascended the throne, ordered a general amnesty, and adopted the reign title Yongxi.
value.literal: That same day the crown prince assumed the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Yongxi.

value.zh: 尊皇后楊氏曰皇太后，立妃賈氏爲皇后。
value.en: Empress Yang was elevated to empress dowager, and his consort Lady Jia was installed as empress.
value.literal: The empress, Lady Yang, was honored as empress dowager; Consort Jia was established as empress.

value.zh: 三月，平東將軍、齊王冏起兵以討倫，傳檄州郡，屯于陽翟。
value.en: In the third month Prince Jiong of Qi, general who pacifies the east, mobilized against Prince Lun, circulated a call to arms through every province, and camped at Yangzhai.
value.literal: In the third month, General Who Pacifies the East, Prince Jiong of Qi, raised troops to attack Lun, transmitted proclamations to the provinces and commanderies, and encamped at Yangzhai.

value.zh: 征北大將軍、成都王穎，征西大將軍、河間王顒，常山王乂，豫州刺史李毅，兗州刺史王彥，南中郎將、新野公歆，皆舉兵應之，眾數十萬。
value.en: Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu and Grand General Who Campaigns North; Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian and Grand General Who Campaigns West; Sima Yi, Prince of Changshan; Li Yi, inspector of Yu Province; Wang Yan, inspector of Yan Province; and Xin, Duke of Xinye and General of the Southern Gentlemen-of-the-Household, all raised armies in response, mustering several hundred thousand men.
value.literal: General-in-chief who conquers the north, Prince Ying of Chengdu; general-in-chief who conquers the west, Prince Yong of Hejian; Prince Yi of Changshan; Inspector of Yu Province Li Yi; Inspector of Yan Province Wang Yan; General of the Southern Gentlemen of the Household, Duke Xin of Xinye—all raised troops in response; the hosts numbered several hundred thousand.

value.zh: 倫遣其將閭和出伊闕，張泓、孫輔出堮阪以距冏，孫會、士猗、許超出黃橋以距穎。
value.en: Prince Lun sent Lü He through the Yique pass, Zhang Hong and Sun Fu over the E ridge to block Prince Jiong, and Sun Hui, Shi Yi, and Xu Chao from Huang Bridge to stop Prince Ying.
value.literal: Lun dispatched his generals Lü He out of Yique, Zhang Hong and Sun Fu out of E Slope to resist Jiong, and Sun Hui, Shi Yi, and Xu Chao out of Huang Bridge to resist Ying.

value.zh: 及穎將趙驤、石超戰于湨水，會等大敗，棄軍走。
value.en: At the Ju River, Zhao Xiang and Shi Chao, serving Prince Ying, routed Sun Hui’s army, which broke and ran.
value.literal: When Ying’s generals Zhao Xiang and Shi Chao battled at the Ju River, Hui and the others were greatly defeated and abandoned the army and fled.

value.zh: 陳騫
value.en: Chen Qian
value.literal: Chen Qian

value.zh: 頠深患時俗放蕩，不尊儒術，何晏、阮籍素有高名於世，口談浮虛，不遵禮法，屍祿耽寵，仕不事事；
value.en: Pei Wei deeply worried that the age's unrestrained customs did not honor Confucian teaching. He Yan and Ruan Ji enjoyed lofty reputations, talking idle emptiness and ignoring ritual law, drawing salary and indulging favor while holding office yet doing nothing.
value.literal: Pei Wei deeply worried that the customs of the age were unrestrained and did not honor Confucian teaching; He Yan and Ruan Ji enjoyed lofty reputations in the world, talking idle emptiness at the mouth and not observing ritual law—drawing salary and indulging favor while holding office yet doing nothing.

value.zh: 至王衍之徒，聲譽太盛，位高勢重，不以物務自嬰，遂相放效，風教陵遲，乃著崇有之論以釋其蔽曰：夫總混群本，宗極之道也。
value.en: When it came to Wang Yan and his followers, their reputations were too great and their positions high and powerful, yet they did not entangle themselves in practical affairs. They then imitated one another, and custom and teaching declined. Pei Wei therefore wrote the Treatise on Honoring Being to explain this harm, saying: Gathering and blending the many roots is the Way that honors the ultimate.
value.literal: When it came to Wang Yan and his followers, their reputations were too great and their positions high and powerful, yet they did not entangle themselves in practical affairs. They then imitated one another, and custom and teaching declined. Pei Wei therefore wrote the Treatise on Honoring Being to explain this harm, saying: Gathering and blending the many roots is the Way that honors the ultimate.

value.zh: 方以族異，庶類之品也。
value.en: Being square or regular differs according to kind; this is the ordering of the many classes.
value.literal: Being square or regular differs according to kind; this is the ordering of the many classes.

value.zh: 形象著分，有生之體也。
value.en: Forms and appearances display distinctions; this is the substance of what has life.
value.literal: Forms and appearances display distinctions; this is the substance of what has life.

value.zh: 化感錯綜，理跡之原也。
value.en: Transformation and response are interwoven; this is the source of the traces of principle.
value.literal: Transformation and response are interwoven; this is the source of the traces of principle.

value.zh: 夫品而為族，則所稟者偏，偏無自足，故憑乎外資。
value.en: When things are ordered into classes and become kinds, what each receives is partial. What is partial cannot suffice by itself, and therefore depends on external resources.
value.literal: When things are ordered into classes and become kinds, what each receives is partial. What is partial cannot suffice by itself, and therefore depends on external resources.

value.zh: 是以生而可尋，所謂理也。
value.en: Thus what can be traced in life is what is called principle.
value.literal: Thus what can be traced in life is what is called principle.

value.zh: 理之所體，所謂有也。
value.en: What principle embodies is what is called being.
value.literal: What principle embodies is what is called being.

value.zh: 有之所須，所謂資也。
value.en: What being requires is what is called resource.
value.literal: What being requires is what is called resource.

value.zh: 資有攸合，所謂宜也。
value.en: When resources have what they fit, this is what is called appropriateness.
value.literal: When resources have what they fit, this is what is called appropriateness.

value.zh: 擇乎厥宜，所謂情也。
value.en: Choosing according to that appropriateness is what is called feeling or disposition.
value.literal: Choosing according to that appropriateness is what is called feeling or disposition.

value.zh: 識智既授，雖出處異業，默語殊塗，所以寶生存宜，其情一也。
value.en: Once perception and intelligence have been granted, even if withdrawal and service are different activities and silence and speech are different paths, the reason one values life and preserves what is appropriate is one in disposition.
value.literal: Once perception and intelligence have been granted, even if withdrawal and service are different activities and silence and speech are different paths, the reason one values life and preserves what is appropriate is one in disposition.

value.zh: 眾理並而無害，故貴賤形焉。
value.en: The many principles coexist without harming one another, and therefore noble and base take shape.
value.literal: The many principles coexist without harming one another, and therefore noble and base take shape.

value.zh: 失得由乎所接，故吉凶兆焉。
value.en: Loss and gain arise from what one engages, and therefore good and bad fortune show their signs.
value.literal: Loss and gain arise from what one engages, and therefore good and bad fortune show their signs.

value.zh: 是以賢人君子，知欲不可絕，而交物有會。
value.en: Therefore worthy men and gentlemen know that desires cannot be cut off, and that engagement with things has its proper meeting point.
value.literal: Therefore worthy men and gentlemen know that desires cannot be cut off, and that engagement with things has its proper meeting point.

value.zh: 觀乎往復，稽中定務。
value.en: They observe going and returning, examine the mean, and settle affairs.
value.literal: They observe going and returning, examine the mean, and settle affairs.

value.zh: 惟夫用天之道，分地之利，躬其力任，勞而後饗。
value.en: Only by using the Way of Heaven, dividing the benefits of Earth, personally taking up one's strength and responsibilities, and laboring before enjoying can things be done.
value.literal: Only by using the Way of Heaven, dividing the benefits of Earth, personally taking up one's strength and responsibilities, and laboring before enjoying can things be done.

value.zh: 居以仁順，守以恭儉，率以忠信，行以敬讓，志無盈求，事無過用，乃可濟乎！
value.en: Dwell in humaneness and compliance, keep to reverence and frugality, lead with loyalty and trustworthiness, act with respect and yielding, let the will have no overflowing demands, and let affairs have no excessive use; only then can one succeed.
value.literal: Dwell in humaneness and compliance, keep to reverence and frugality, lead with loyalty and trustworthiness, act with respect and yielding, let the will have no overflowing demands, and let affairs have no excessive use; only then can one succeed.

value.zh: 故大建厥極，綏理群生，訓物垂範，於是乎在，斯則聖人為政之由也。
value.en: Thus greatly establishing the standard, pacifying and ordering the multitude of living beings, instructing things and leaving models depend on this; this is the route by which the sages carried out government.
value.literal: Thus greatly establishing the standard, pacifying and ordering the multitude of living beings, instructing things and leaving models depend on this; this is the route by which the sages carried out government.

value.zh: 若乃淫抗陵肆，則危害萌矣。
value.en: If, however, excess, resistance, arrogance, and unrestrained conduct arise, danger and harm begin to sprout.
value.literal: If, however, excess, resistance, arrogance, and unrestrained conduct arise, danger and harm begin to sprout.

value.zh: 故欲衍則速患，情佚則怨博，擅恣則興攻，專利則延寇，可謂以厚生而失生者也。
value.en: Thus when desire spreads it hastens trouble; when feeling is indulgent resentments broaden; when one acts arbitrarily and willfully attacks arise; when one monopolizes benefit bandits are invited. This may be called losing life while trying to enrich life.
value.literal: Thus when desire spreads it hastens trouble; when feeling is indulgent resentments broaden; when one acts arbitrarily and willfully attacks arise; when one monopolizes benefit bandits are invited. This may be called losing life while trying to enrich life.

value.zh: 悠悠之徒，駭乎若茲之釁，而尋艱爭所緣。
value.en: The drifting sort of people were startled by troubles like these and sought out the causes from which hardship and contention arose.
value.literal: The drifting sort of people were startled by troubles like these and sought out the causes from which hardship and contention arose.

value.zh: 察夫偏質有弊，而睹簡損之善，遂闡貴無之議，而建賤有之論。
value.en: They observed that partial substance has defects, and saw the good in simplicity and reduction; they then expounded the doctrine that honors nonbeing and established the argument that devalues being.
value.literal: They observed that partial substance has defects, and saw the good in simplicity and reduction; they then expounded the doctrine that honors nonbeing and established the argument that devalues being.

value.zh: 賤有則必外形，外形則必遺制，遺制則必忽防，忽防則必忘禮。
value.en: If being is devalued, then form must be externalized; if form is externalized, then institutions must be abandoned; if institutions are abandoned, then safeguards must be neglected; if safeguards are neglected, then ritual must be forgotten.
value.literal: If being is devalued, then form must be externalized; if form is externalized, then institutions must be abandoned; if institutions are abandoned, then safeguards must be neglected; if safeguards are neglected, then ritual must be forgotten.

value.zh: 禮制弗存，則無以為政矣。
value.en: If ritual institutions do not remain, there is nothing by which to govern.
value.literal: If ritual institutions do not remain, there is nothing by which to govern.

value.zh: 眾之從上，猶水之居器也。
value.en: The multitude following those above is like water occupying a vessel.
value.literal: The multitude following those above is like water occupying a vessel.

value.zh: 故兆庶之情，信于所習；
value.en: Therefore the feelings of the common people trust in what they are accustomed to.
value.literal: Therefore the feelings of the common people trust in what they are accustomed to.

value.zh: 習則心服其業，業服則謂之理然。
value.en: Once accustomed, their minds submit to their tasks; when their tasks are accepted, they call it naturally right.
value.literal: Once accustomed, their minds submit to their tasks; when their tasks are accepted, they call it naturally right.

value.zh: 是以君人必慎所教，班其政刑一切之務，分宅百姓，各授四職，能令稟命之者不肅而安，忽然忘異，莫有遷志。
value.en: Therefore one who rules people must be careful about what he teaches, distributes all the affairs of government and punishments, divides dwellings among the hundred surnames, and assigns each of the four occupations. He can make those who receive commands be at ease without sternness, suddenly forget differences, and have no mind to shift.
value.literal: Therefore one who rules people must be careful about what he teaches, distributes all the affairs of government and punishments, divides dwellings among the hundred surnames, and assigns each of the four occupations. He can make those who receive commands be at ease without sternness, suddenly forget differences, and have no mind to shift.

value.zh: 況於據在三之尊，懷所隆之情，敦以為訓者哉！
value.en: How much more is this true for one who occupies the honor of the three (ruler, father, and teacher), holds feelings about what should be exalted, and treats them seriously as instruction.
value.literal: How much more is this true for one who occupies the honor of the three (ruler, father, and teacher), holds feelings about what should be exalted, and treats them seriously as instruction.

value.zh: 斯乃昏明所階，不可不審。
value.en: This is the step by which darkness or clarity proceeds, and it must be examined carefully.
value.literal: This is the step by which darkness or clarity proceeds, and it must be examined carefully.

value.zh: 夫盈欲可損而未可絕有也，過用可節而未可謂無貴也。
value.en: Overflowing desire may be reduced, but being cannot be cut off; excessive use may be regulated, but it cannot be said that there is nothing valuable.
value.literal: Overflowing desire may be reduced, but being cannot be cut off; excessive use may be regulated, but it cannot be said that there is nothing valuable.

value.zh: 蓋有講言之具者，深列有形之故，盛稱空無之美。
value.en: Those equipped for discourse deeply arrayed the causes of what has form and grandly praised the beauty of emptiness and nonbeing.
value.literal: Those equipped for discourse deeply arrayed the causes of what has form and grandly praised the beauty of emptiness and nonbeing.

value.zh: 形器之故有征，空無之義難檢，辯巧之文可悅，似象之言足惑，眾聽眩焉，溺其成說。
value.en: The causes of forms and vessels have evidence; the meaning of emptiness and nonbeing is hard to check. Cleverly argued writings can delight, and words resembling images are enough to confuse, so the many listeners were dazzled and drowned in these completed doctrines.
value.literal: The causes of forms and vessels have evidence; the meaning of emptiness and nonbeing is hard to check. Cleverly argued writings can delight, and words resembling images are enough to confuse, so the many listeners were dazzled and drowned in these completed doctrines.

value.zh: 雖頗有異此心者，辭不獲濟，屈於所狎，因謂虛無之理，誠不可蓋。
value.en: Although some had minds that differed from this, their words could not prevail; they yielded to what was familiar, and accordingly said that the principle of emptiness and nonbeing truly could not be covered over.
value.literal: Although some had minds that differed from this, their words could not prevail; they yielded to what was familiar, and accordingly said that the principle of emptiness and nonbeing truly could not be covered over.

value.zh: 唱而有和，多往弗反，遂薄綜世之務，賤功烈之用，高浮游之業，埤經實之賢。
value.en: When one sang out, others harmonized; many went forth and did not return. They then slighted the work of managing the age, devalued the use of achievements, elevated the occupation of drifting idly, and lowered worthies of canonical substance.
value.literal: When one sang out, others harmonized; many went forth and did not return. They then slighted the work of managing the age, devalued the use of achievements, elevated the occupation of drifting idly, and lowered worthies of canonical substance.

value.zh: 人情所殉，篤夫名利。
value.en: What human feelings die for is especially name and profit.
value.literal: What human feelings die for is especially name and profit.

value.zh: 於是文者衍其辭，訥者贊其旨，染其眾也。
value.en: Thereupon those skilled in writing elaborated their words, and those slow of speech praised their intent, staining the multitude with it.
value.literal: Thereupon those skilled in writing elaborated their words, and those slow of speech praised their intent, staining the multitude with it.

value.zh: 是以立言藉於虛無，謂之玄妙；
value.en: Thus setting up words by relying on emptiness and nonbeing was called mysterious subtlety.
value.literal: Thus setting up words by relying on emptiness and nonbeing was called mysterious subtlety.

value.zh: 處官不親所司，謂之雅遠；
value.en: Holding office without personally attending to one's responsibilities was called elegant remoteness.
value.literal: Holding office without personally attending to one's responsibilities was called elegant remoteness.

value.zh: 奉身散其廉操，謂之曠達。
value.en: Supporting oneself while scattering one's integrity and conduct was called broad-minded freedom.
value.literal: Supporting oneself while scattering one's integrity and conduct was called broad-minded freedom.

value.zh: 故砥礪之風，彌以陵遲。
value.en: Therefore the custom of whetting and disciplining oneself declined all the more.
value.literal: Therefore the custom of whetting and disciplining oneself declined all the more.

value.zh: 放者因斯，或悖吉凶之禮，而忽容止之表，瀆棄長幼之序，混漫貴賤之級。
value.en: The unrestrained used this as their basis, sometimes violating the rituals of auspicious and inauspicious occasions, neglecting the outward signs of bearing and deportment, profaning and abandoning the order of elder and younger, and confusing and blurring the ranks of noble and base.
value.literal: The unrestrained used this as their basis, sometimes violating the rituals of auspicious and inauspicious occasions, neglecting the outward signs of bearing and deportment, profaning and abandoning the order of elder and younger, and confusing and blurring the ranks of noble and base.

value.zh: 其甚者至於裸裎，言笑忘宜，以不惜為弘，士行又虧矣。
value.en: The worst of them even reached naked exposure, forgot what was proper in speech and laughter, took lack of restraint as magnanimity, and gentlemanly conduct was further damaged.
value.literal: The worst of them even reached naked exposure, forgot what was proper in speech and laughter, took lack of restraint as magnanimity, and gentlemanly conduct was further damaged.

value.zh: 老子既著五千之文，表摭穢雜之弊，甄舉靜一之義，有以令人釋然自夷，合于《易》之《損》、《謙》、《艮》、《節》之旨。
value.en: Laozi wrote the text of five thousand words, displayed and picked out the harms of filth and mixture, and selected and raised the meaning of stillness and unity, so that people could be released and level themselves. This accords with the meanings of Decrease, Modesty, Keeping Still, and Regulation in the Changes.
value.literal: Laozi wrote the text of five thousand words, displayed and picked out the harms of filth and mixture, and selected and raised the meaning of stillness and unity, so that people could be released and level themselves. This accords with the meanings of Decrease, Modesty, Keeping Still, and Regulation in the Changes.

value.zh: 而靜一守本，無虛無之謂也；
value.en: But stillness, unity, and guarding the root do not mean emptiness and nonbeing.
value.literal: But stillness, unity, and guarding the root do not mean emptiness and nonbeing.

value.zh: 《損》《艮》之屬，蓋君子之一道，非《易》之所以為體守本無也。
value.en: Decrease, Keeping Still, and the like are one way of the gentleman; they are not the way by which the Changes makes guarding root nonbeing its substance.
value.literal: Decrease, Keeping Still, and the like are one way of the gentleman; they are not the way by which the Changes makes guarding root nonbeing its substance.

value.zh: 觀老子之書雖博有所經，而云「有生於無」，以虛為主，偏立一家之辭，豈有以而然哉！
value.en: Looking at Laozi's book, although it broadly passes through many things, it says, "Being is born from nonbeing," takes emptiness as its master, and partially establishes the words of one school. How could there be a sufficient reason for this?
value.literal: Looking at Laozi's book, although it broadly passes through many things, it says, "Being is born from nonbeing," takes emptiness as its master, and partially establishes the words of one school. How could there be a sufficient reason for this?

value.zh: 人之既生，以保生為全，全之所階，以順感為務。
value.en: Once people have been born, they take preserving life as wholeness; the step to wholeness takes responding in accord as its task.
value.literal: Once people have been born, they take preserving life as wholeness; the step to wholeness takes responding in accord as its task.

value.zh: 若味近以虧業，則沈溺之釁興；
value.en: If one savors what is near and thereby damages one's work, then the trouble of sinking and drowning arises.
value.literal: If one savors what is near and thereby damages one's work, then the trouble of sinking and drowning arises.

value.zh: 懷末以忘本，則天理之真滅。
value.en: If one cherishes the branch and forgets the root, then the truth of heavenly principle is extinguished.
value.literal: If one cherishes the branch and forgets the root, then the truth of heavenly principle is extinguished.

value.zh: 故動之所交，存亡之會也。
value.en: Therefore what action engages is the meeting point of survival and ruin.
value.literal: Therefore what action engages is the meeting point of survival and ruin.

value.zh: 夫有非有，於無非無；
value.en: Being is not merely being; in relation to nonbeing it is not nonbeing.
value.literal: Being is not merely being; in relation to nonbeing it is not nonbeing.

value.zh: 于無非無，於有非有。
value.en: In relation to nonbeing it is not nonbeing, and in relation to being it is not merely being.
value.literal: In relation to nonbeing it is not nonbeing, and in relation to being it is not merely being.

value.zh: 是以申縱播之累，而著貴無之文。
value.en: Therefore Laozi extended the harms of indulgence and diffusion, and wrote a text that honored nonbeing.
value.literal: Therefore Laozi extended the harms of indulgence and diffusion, and wrote a text that honored nonbeing.

value.zh: 將以絕所非之盈謬，存大善之中節，收流遁於既過，反澄正於胸懷。
value.en: He was about to cut off the overflowing errors he rejected, preserve the central measure of great goodness, gather back what had flowed away after going too far, and return clarity and correctness to the breast.
value.literal: He was about to cut off the overflowing errors he rejected, preserve the central measure of great goodness, gather back what had flowed away after going too far, and return clarity and correctness to the breast.

value.zh: 宜其以無為辭，而旨在全有，故其辭曰「以為文不足」。
value.en: It is fitting that he used nonbeing as his wording while his intent lay in making being whole; therefore his words say, "I consider writing insufficient."
value.literal: It is fitting that he used nonbeing as his wording while his intent lay in making being whole; therefore his words say, "I consider writing insufficient."

value.zh: 若斯，則是所寄之塗，一方之言也。
value.en: If it is like this, then this is a path on which something was lodged, the words of one side.
value.literal: If it is like this, then this is a path on which something was lodged, the words of one side.

value.zh: 若謂至理信以無為宗，則偏而害當矣。
value.en: If one says that the highest principle truly takes nonbeing as its ancestor, then this is partial and harms what is appropriate.
value.literal: If one says that the highest principle truly takes nonbeing as its ancestor, then this is partial and harms what is appropriate.

value.zh: 先賢達識，以非所滯，示之深論。
value.en: Earlier worthies of penetrating understanding, because they were not stuck there, showed this in deep arguments.
value.literal: Earlier worthies of penetrating understanding, because they were not stuck there, showed this in deep arguments.

value.zh: 惟班固著難，未足折其情。
value.en: Only Ban Gu wrote objections, but they were not sufficient to break its appeal.
value.literal: Only Ban Gu wrote objections, but they were not sufficient to break its appeal.

value.zh: 孫卿、楊雄大體抑之，猶偏有所許。
value.en: Xunzi and Yang Xiong suppressed it in general outline, yet still partly allowed it.
value.literal: Xunzi and Yang Xiong suppressed it in general outline, yet still partly allowed it.

value.zh: 而虛無之言，日以廣衍，眾家扇起，各列其說。
value.en: But the words of emptiness and nonbeing spread more widely day by day, and the many schools stirred one another up, each setting forth its theory.
value.literal: But the words of emptiness and nonbeing spread more widely day by day, and the many schools stirred one another up, each setting forth its theory.

value.zh: 上及造化，下被萬事，莫不貴無，所存僉同。
value.en: Above they reached creation and transformation, below they covered the ten thousand affairs; there was nothing in which they did not honor nonbeing, and what they preserved was all the same.
value.literal: Above they reached creation and transformation, below they covered the ten thousand affairs; there was nothing in which they did not honor nonbeing, and what they preserved was all the same.

value.zh: 情以眾固，乃號凡有之理皆義之埤者，薄而鄙焉。
value.en: Because feeling was made firm by the crowd, they then called every principle of being a low supplement to meaning and treated it as slight and contemptible.
value.literal: Because feeling was made firm by the crowd, they then called every principle of being a low supplement to meaning and treated it as slight and contemptible.

value.zh: 辯論人倫及經明之業，遂易門肆。
value.en: Debating human relations and the work of making the classics clear accordingly changed gates and marketplaces.
value.literal: Debating human relations and the work of making the classics clear accordingly changed gates and marketplaces.

value.zh: 頠用矍然，申其所懷，而攻者盈集。
value.en: Pei Wei therefore became alarmed and expressed what he held in mind, but attackers gathered in numbers.
value.literal: Pei Wei therefore became alarmed and expressed what he held in mind, but attackers gathered in numbers.

value.zh: 或以為一時口言。
value.en: Some thought it was only words spoken for the moment.
value.literal: Some thought it was only words spoken for the moment.

value.zh: 有客幸過，咸見命著文，擿列虛無不允之征。
value.en: When guests happened to visit, all urged him to write an essay and pick out and list the proofs that emptiness and nonbeing were not sound.
value.literal: When guests happened to visit, all urged him to write an essay and pick out and list the proofs that emptiness and nonbeing were not sound.

value.zh: 若未能每事釋正，則無家之義弗可奪也。
value.en: If he could not explain and correct each matter, then the meaning of the school of nonbeing could not be seized away.
value.literal: If he could not explain and correct each matter, then the meaning of the school of nonbeing could not be seized away.

value.zh: 頠退而思之，雖君子宅情，無求於顯，及其立言，在乎達旨而已。
value.en: Pei Wei withdrew and thought about it. Although a gentleman lodges his feelings and does not seek display, when it comes to establishing words, it only lies in making the intent clear.
value.literal: Pei Wei withdrew and thought about it. Although a gentleman lodges his feelings and does not seek display, when it comes to establishing words, it only lies in making the intent clear.
